lead: A cantilever slab is fixed along one edge and free at the other: a balcony, a chajja over a window, a canopy. Its moment is hogging at the support, so the main steel is at the top and must be anchored well behind the support. A continuous slab runs over three or more supports; IS 456 gives its design moments and shears as coefficients (Tables 12 and 13) that already allow for live load on some spans and not others. Both are designed as 1 m strips, like a one-way slab.
prereq: You need One-way slabs (effective span, Ast, minimum steel, deflection factor).

blocks.text: Under load a cantilever bends down and its top fibre stretches, so the tension steel sits near the top face. The moment is largest at the face of the support: for a uniform factored load w<sub>u</sub> over the clear projection l and a line load P<sub>u</sub> at the free edge (a railing or parapet),

blocks.where: M<sub>u</sub> in kN·m per metre at the face of the support; l is the clear projection in m; P<sub>u</sub> in kN/m.

items: Effective span for deflection (cl. 22.2 c): the length to the face of the support plus d/2. The basic span/d is 7, times the Fig. 4 factor. Cantilevers are usually decided by this check.
Shear is checked at a distance d from the face: V<sub>u</sub> = w<sub>u</sub>(l − d) + P<sub>u</sub>.

The top bars run back into the slab or beam behind the support by at least the development length L<sub>d</sub> = φσ<sub>s</sub>/(4τ<sub>bd</sub>), with τ<sub>bd</sub> = 1.2 × 1.6 = 1.92 N/mm² for deformed bars in M20: L<sub>d</sub> = 47φ for Fe415.
The back span or the supporting beam must hold the cantilever down: a balcony on a beam twists that beam, so the beam needs torsion design.
Distribution steel (minimum steel) runs along the support, tied under the top main bars.

sections.h3: Continuous slabs and the moment coefficients

blocks.text: In a slab over many beams the worst moment at each section comes from a different live-load pattern: the largest sagging moment in a span when that span and alternate spans carry live load; the largest hogging moment at a support when the two spans next to it are loaded, with the rest following alternately. Dead load is always everywhere. For uniform loads cl. 22.5 lets the designer skip this and use coefficients, if there are at least three spans that differ by no more than 15 % of the longest.

blocks.where: w<sub>D</sub> and w<sub>L</sub> are the factored dead and live loads in kN/m on the strip; l is the effective span (for a support moment, the mean of the two spans). Table 13 gives shears the same way: 0.4 w<sub>D</sub> l and 0.45 w<sub>L</sub> l at the end support; 0.6 for both on the outer side of the support next to it.

blocks.text: Moments found by coefficients may not be redistributed. The steel follows the moment envelope: bottom bars in every span, top bars over every support, the heaviest at the first interior support. A continuous slab uses the basic span/d of 26.

examples.question: Design a balcony slab projecting 1.2 m clear from the face of a beam. Live load 3 kN/m², floor finish 1 kN/m², railing 1 kN/m at the free edge. M20, Fe415, 20 mm cover, 10 mm bars.
steps: Trial D = 140 mm, d = 140 − 20 − 5 = 115 mm. (With D = 130 mm the deflection check fails: l/d = 11.93 against 11.17.)
Loads: self weight 3.50 + 1.0 + 3.0 = 7.50 kN/m², w<sub>u</sub> = 11.250 kN/m²; P<sub>u</sub> = 1.5 × 1.0 = 1.5 kN/m.

Steel: 4.6 M<sub>u</sub>/(f<sub>ck</sub> b d²) = 0.1722; A<sub>st</sub> = 250 mm²/m (minimum 168). 10 mm bars: 1000 × 78.54/250 = 314 mm, limited to 300 mm. Provide 10 mm @ 300 mm c/c at the top (262 mm²/m).
Deflection: effective span 1.2 + 0.0575 = 1.2575 m, l/d = 10.93. f<sub>s</sub> = 0.58 × 415 × 250/262 = 230 N/mm², p<sub>t</sub> = 0.228 %, factor ≈ 1.77, allowed 7 × 1.77 = 12.41. Safe.
Shear at d from the face: V<sub>u</sub> = 11.250 × (1.2 − 0.115) + 1.5 = 13.71 kN/m, τ<sub>v</sub> = 0.119 N/mm² < kτ<sub>c</sub> = 1.30 × 0.342 = 0.445 N/mm². Safe.
Anchorage: L<sub>d</sub> = 10 × 0.87 × 415/(4 × 1.92) = 470 mm; run the top bars at least 470 mm beyond the face into the floor slab behind.
Distribution steel: 168 mm²/m, 8 mm @ 290 mm c/c along the support, under the top bars.
examples.answer: D = 140 mm; top bars 10 mm @ 300 mm c/c, M<sub>u</sub> = 9.90 kN·m/m, anchored 470 mm behind the face; distribution 8 mm @ 290 mm.

examples.question: A one-way slab is continuous over five beams (four equal spans) at 3.5 m centres; beams are 230 mm wide. D = 130 mm, d = 105 mm, floor finish 1 kN/m², live load 3 kN/m², M20, Fe415. Find the design moments by IS 456 Table 12 and the steel.
steps: Clear span 3.27 m; 230 mm < 272 mm (1/12 of the clear span), so l = smaller of 3.27 + 0.105 and 3.5 = 3.375 m.
Factored loads: w<sub>D</sub> = 1.5 × (3.25 + 1.0) = 6.375 kN/m; w<sub>L</sub> = 1.5 × 3.0 = 4.5 kN/m; l² = 11.391 m².
Middle of end span: M<sub>u</sub> = +(1/12 × 6.375 + 1/10 × 4.5) × 11.391 = +11.18 kN·m/m; A<sub>st</sub> = 315 mm²/m; 10 mm @ 240 mm bottom (327 mm²/m).
Support next to the end support: M<sub>u</sub> = −(1/10 × 6.375 + 1/9 × 4.5) × 11.391 = −12.96 kN·m/m; A<sub>st</sub> = 369 mm²/m; 10 mm @ 210 mm top (374 mm²/m).
Middle of interior span: M<sub>u</sub> = +(1/16 × 6.375 + 1/12 × 4.5) × 11.391 = +8.81 kN·m/m; A<sub>st</sub> = 244 mm²/m; 10 mm @ 300 mm bottom (262 mm²/m).
Other interior supports: M<sub>u</sub> = −(1/12 × 6.375 + 1/9 × 4.5) × 11.391 = −11.75 kN·m/m; A<sub>st</sub> = 332 mm²/m; 10 mm @ 230 mm top (341 mm²/m).
Shear (Table 13), outer side of the support next to the end: V<sub>u</sub> = (0.6 × 6.375 + 0.6 × 4.5) × 3.375 = 22.02 kN/m; τ<sub>v</sub> = 0.210 N/mm² < 1.30 × 0.411 = 0.534 N/mm².
Deflection, end span: l/d = 32.1; p<sub>t</sub> = 0.31 %, factor ≈ 1.53; allowed 26 × 1.53 = 39.7. Safe.
examples.answer: Largest moment −12.96 kN·m/m at the first interior support (10 mm @ 210 top); end spans 10 mm @ 240 bottom; interior spans 10 mm @ 300 bottom; other supports 10 mm @ 230 top.

traps: Putting cantilever main steel at the bottom. The tension is at the top; bottom bars there do nothing and the slab cracks at the support.
Stopping the top bars at the face of the support. They need L<sub>d</sub> = 470 mm (47φ) beyond the face, or the bar pulls out before it yields.
Leaving out the railing or parapet load at the tip: it has the full lever arm l.
Using the coefficients for two spans, unequal spans (more than 15 % apart) or heavy point loads. Analyse those with pattern loading.
Using the same coefficient for dead and live load. Live load gets the larger value (1/10 against 1/12 at the end span) because it may be on some spans only.

quiz.q: Where is the main steel of a cantilever slab, and why?
quiz.a: Near the top face, because the hogging moment at the support stretches the top fibre.

quiz.q: State the conditions for using the IS 456 moment coefficients.
quiz.a: Uniform load, at least three spans, spans not differing by more than 15 % of the longest; no redistribution of the resulting moments.

quiz.q: Why does live load get a larger coefficient than dead load in Table 12?
quiz.a: Live load can be on some spans and not others; the worst patterns give larger moments than load on all spans, while dead load is always everywhere.

quiz.q: A chajja projects 0.6 m clear, D = 100 mm, finish 0.5 kN/m², live load 0.75 kN/m². Find M<sub>u</sub> at the face.
For four continuous spans, which spans carry live load for the largest sagging moment in span 2?
quiz.a: Spans 2 and 4 (alternate spans), with dead load on all four.

quiz.q: Why does loading spans 1 and 3 reduce the hogging moment at the support between spans 1 and 2 compared with loading spans 1 and 2?
quiz.a: Load on span 3 lifts span 2 near support B (the influence of a load alternates in sign from span to span), which reduces the hogging at B; loading the two spans next to B makes both rotate the slab the same way at B and gives the maximum.

quiz.q: A designer measures a 1.2 m balcony to the centre of a 300 mm beam. Effect?
quiz.a: The span becomes 1.35 m and M<sub>u</sub> rises by about (1.35/1.2)² ≈ 1.27 times for the uniform part: safe but wasteful, and it hides that the critical section and anchorage start at the face.

beyond: Not for the exam. Long balconies are often made with a downstand edge beam or as precast units with thermal-break connectors that stop heat leaking through the slab. Continuous slabs in practice are analysed with frame or finite element software with pattern loading, and the coefficients serve as a check. Search for "thermal break balcony" and "moment redistribution in continuous slabs".

figure.caption: Top: the balcony carries 12.0 kN/m and a 1.5 kN/m railing load at its tip, so the face of the beam takes a hogging moment of 9.90 kN·m per metre; the top bars run 470 mm (47φ) past the face. Bottom: the Table 12 moments of the four-span slab, largest at the first interior supports.
